diagnosis: Calibration NSE is 0.68 (KGE 0.78, PBIAS about 0%) for 1971–1997. On 1989–1997, run as a separate check, NSE is 0.69 and PBIAS is -1%, so performance looks stable over time. This is a regulated catchment: the Loch Lyon and Loch an Daimh hydro reservoirs divert water. Observed runoff (about 2.65 mm/d) is far below precipitation minus PET (about 4.6 mm/d), so the standard HBV water balance cannot close. I closed it with two non-physical choices. First, PERC (about 6.7 mm/d) drains the upper zone into a lower store that acts as a near-permanent sink (K2 = 1e-6). This mimics the hydro intakes capturing flow up to a capacity limit. Second, that lower store starts at 1e6 mm, so it releases an almost constant baseflow of about 1 mm/d, standing in for compensation flows. Its level drifted only about 1% over 27 years, so the setup does not change over time. SFCF (about 0.4) also removes some snow water. Weaknesses: floods are smoothed by the reservoirs and diversions, so peaks are underestimated (simulated maximum 42 vs 60 mm/d observed). Low flows are simulated as a flat constant. Snow and the soil parameters (FC about 790, BETA about 0.5) are only loosely identifiable. I trust the water balance and the stable timing, but the parameters are compensating for missing regulation processes, so the individual values have little physical meaning.
